'''William Alfred Massey''' is an American mathematician and [[operations research]]er, the Edwin S. Wilsey Professor of Operations Research and Financial Engineering at [[Princeton University]]. He is an expert in [[queueing theory]].

==Biography==
Massey was born in [[Jefferson City, Missouri]] in 1956,<ref name="Buffalo">{{cite web|title=William A. Massey|url=http://www.math.buffalo.edu/mad/PEEPS/massey_william.html|website=Mathematicians of the African diaspora| publisher=State University of New York at Buffalo|access-date=16 April 2017}}</ref> the son of Juliette and Richard Massey Sr., both educators.
His family moved to [[St. Louis, Missouri]] when he was four.<ref name="mentorship"/> He went to college at [[Princeton University]], graduating in 1977.<ref name="mentorship"/> Massey obtained his Ph.D. from [[Stanford University]] in 1981, with a thesis on [[queueing theory]] supervised by [[Joseph Keller]].<ref>{{mathgenealogy|name=William Alfred Massey|id=30201}}.</ref> His first research publication was developed during a summer program at [[Bell Laboratories]] while he was a graduate student and was published in 1978. After earning his doctorate, he became a permanent staff member at Bell Labs.<ref name=" mentorship"/> In 2001, Massey moved to his current position at Princeton, becoming the first African-American Princeton undergraduate alumnus to return as a faculty member.<ref name="mentorship"/>

==Awards and honors==
In 2006, Massey won the Blackwell–Tapia Prize of the [[Institute for Mathematics and its Applications]] for his "outstanding record of achievement in mathematical research and his mentoring of minorities and women in the field of mathematics".<ref name="mentorship">{{citation |url=https://www.princeton.edu/main/news/archive/S16/16/11S55/index.xml?section=featured |title=Massey's mentorship creates network of mathematicians|newspaper=Princeton Weekly Bulletin|date=October 23, 2006}}.</ref> He was elected to the 2006 class of [[Fellow]]s of the [[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]].<ref>{{citation|url=https://www.informs.org/Recognizing-Excellence/Fellows/Fellows-Alphabetical-List|title=Fellows: Alphabetical List|publisher=[[Institute for Operations Research and the Management Sciences]]|access-date=2019-10-09}}</ref> In 2012 he became a fellow of the [[American Mathematical Society]].<ref>[http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list List of Fellows of the American Mathematical Society] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180825194636/http://www.ams.org/profession/fellows-list |date=2018-08-25 }}, retrieved 2013-02-02.</ref> Massey's accomplishments have earned him recognition by [[Mathematically Gifted & Black]] as a Black History Month 2018 Honoree.<ref>{{Cite web|title=William A. Massey |url=https://mathematicallygiftedandblack.com/honorees/william-a-massey/|access-date=|website=Mathematically Gifted & Black}}</ref>
